short_summary: The Israeli government has mandated a 2.6 billion shekel budget cut across all ministries to prioritize defense spending. This decision has sparked significant concern among civil service leaders regarding the future of public health, education, and welfare services.

sources.name: Ynet
sources.title: בלי לגעת בכספים הקואליציוניים: משרדי הממשלה זועמים על קיצוץ 2.6 מיליארד שקל עבור מערכת הביטחון

paragraphs: The Israeli government has recently mandated a substantial budgetary reallocation, requiring a 2.6 billion shekel reduction across all government ministries to prioritize urgent defense procurement. This decision, occurring just nine days before national elections, represents the second major fiscal contraction within a single week. While the previous cut of one billion shekels—intended for the purchase of twelve Apache helicopters—was sourced entirely from the multi-year development budget for the Arab sector, this new measure is a 'flat cut.' It imposes a uniform 5% reduction on the flexible budgets of every ministry, specifically targeting funds not earmarked for salaries or rigid state obligations.

Despite recommendations from senior Treasury professionals to utilize coalition funds, the government has explicitly excluded them from these cuts. Treasury officials noted that because several ministries resisted specific reductions, the cabinet opted for this uniform approach. This decision has sparked significant concern, as it directly impacts civil services already under immense strain. The Ministry of Education faces a 285 million shekel reduction. While the ministry confirmed that core teaching hours for schools and kindergartens remain protected, the cut will likely affect extracurricular activities, youth movements, and external educational programs. Officials are currently evaluating how to absorb these losses without compromising essential operations.

Public health officials have expressed profound alarm. Moshe Bar Siman Tov, the Director-General of the Ministry of Health, warned that this latest reduction brings the total deficit in health funding to 600 million shekels since the beginning of 2026. He argued that the systematic erosion of civil infrastructure undermines national resilience, which relies on more than just military strength. According to the ministry, these cuts threaten to exacerbate waiting times and limit access to critical services, particularly in mental health, where demand has surged due to the ongoing conflict. Bar Siman Tov emphasized that the state's ability to function during emergencies depends heavily on the stability of these civil systems.

Similarly, the Ministry of Welfare faces a 140 million shekel reduction. This development is expected to hinder the implementation of vital services for vulnerable populations, including women escaping violence, individuals with disabilities, and women in prostitution. Welfare officials noted that their capacity to address growing social needs has been severely constrained by a series of cuts throughout 2026, totaling 450 million shekels. Conversely, the Ministry of National Security, which faces a 225 million shekel cut, has indicated that the impact will be mitigated. A spokesperson stated that the funds would be drawn from emergency reserves rather than operational budgets, ensuring that police and security activities remain unaffected. Critics of the government's policy continue to argue that placing the burden of defense funding on civil services compromises the long-term stability of the state.

facts.fact: The Israeli government approved a 2.6 billion shekel budget cut across all ministries to fund urgent defense procurement.
The education ministry faces a 285 million shekel cut, while the health ministry faces 150 million, and the welfare ministry faces 140 million.
The Ministry of National Security faces a 225 million shekel cut, which officials claim will come from emergency funds rather than operational budgets.
Coalition funds were excluded from these budget cuts.
